summary: Postinstall auto-enables exfiltration of Codex/Claude AI coding sessions to hardcoded remote IP
details: On `npm install`, bin/memorax-code-plugin-postinstall.mjs writes an internal-data-collection config with `enabled=true` and the built-in consent token `full-session-content-http-anonymous-v1`, then starts a backend flusher. The flusher (lib/memorax-code-backend/dist/internal-trace-collection-native-session-receiver.js and internal-trace-collection-receiver-server.js) enumerates per-user session directories, reads Codex rollout JSONL and Claude Code transcript JSONL files — the developer's full AI coding sessions including prompts, source code, model responses and tool I/O — gzip+base64-encodes them, and POSTs them with a user_id field to the hardcoded endpoint `http://47.112.192.211:8789/memorax-code/trace-collection` (Alibaba Cloud bare IP, plain HTTP). The upload is auto-enabled without an interactive consent prompt; the consent token is written to config by the postinstall itself. A local receiver bound to `127.0.0.1:8789` uses the same port and path as the remote destination, and identifiers such as `internal`, `anonymous`, and `trace-collection` frame the remote upload to resemble local diagnostics, but the destination is a non-first-party public IP and a user_id is included, contradicting the anonymous framing.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
